Light rain likely in 7 districts today:Garba revellers may get wet during final Navratri nights; rain may continue in these cities tomorrow
- Copy link
Amid the heat in Ahmedabad and across the state, the weather is likely to change. The Meteorological Department has forecast that light rain may occur in parts of South Gujarat and Saurashtra over the next two days from today as a cyclonic circulation becomes active.
While the heatwave continues, temperatures may also change in the coming days owing to the forecast of light rain. Garba enthusiasts may get wet during the final nights of Navratri as light to moderate rain has been forecast.
Rain possible due to formation of two cyclonic circulations
Scientist Pradeep Sharma said that, in terms of the weather system, a cyclonic circulation has formed at an altitude of 1.5 km above sea level over southern Rajasthan and adjoining areas. In addition, another cyclonic circulation has formed over the southwestern Arabian Sea, extending up to 5.8 km above sea level. Under its influence, a low-pressure area is likely to form over the southwestern Arabian Sea around 19 October.
No significant change in minimum temperature
“Apart from this, the weather in the state is expected to remain mainly dry for now. There is unlikely to be any significant change in the maximum or minimum temperatures over the next seven days. No warning has currently been issued to fishermen along the Gujarat coast regarding wind speed. However, westerly to north-westerly winds are likely to blow along the north Gujarat coast, while north-easterly winds are expected in south Gujarat.”
4 degrees above normal, people experiencing heat
With temperatures currently above normal across the state, people are experiencing unbearable heat. Rajkot recorded the state's highest maximum temperature at 40.3 degrees Celsius, which is 4 degrees above normal. Besides this, temperatures stood at 39.3 degrees Celsius in Surendranagar, 38.7 in Deesa, 38.6 in Bhuj, 38.4 in Junagadh, 38.2 in Naliya, 37.5 in Surat, 37.2 in Vadodara, 37 in Ahmedabad and 36.7 in Bhavnagar. Temperatures ranging from 31.2 to 36 degrees Celsius were also recorded in areas including Gandhinagar, Porbandar, Kandla, Daman, Diu, Veraval, Okha and Dwarka, keeping the mercury high across the state.
